Julia Ballmann, “Pppanik” liquid-chrome numerals

The numerals “2009” drawn as melted, iridescent chrome blobs, alone on a black square.

Source
AIGA Eye on Design (5 September 2019): “Acid Graphics” Are the New Psychedelia
Creator
Julia Ballmann
Made
Not stated. The caption reads “Pppanik, 2009”, and “2009” is also the content of the image, so the year may be the title, not the date.
Style
Acid graphics (agent-proposed, not yet reviewed by a person)
Moods
Fluid, synthetic, dreamlike
Evidence
Inspected the 1200 px image Julia-Ballmann-Pppanik-2009.jpg that Eye on Design published with the article, in a scratch folder. Not stored. The object is a digital image as the magazine published it, not a named physical copy. The caption reads “Julia Ballmann, Pppanik, 2009”.
Reviewed
2 October 2026
Rights
Link and metadata only. License: unverified. Rights policy

Context

Eye on Design shows the image in its 2019 article on acid graphics, with the caption “Julia Ballmann, Pppanik, 2009”.

Observed

  • Four numerals, “2009”, sit in the middle of a square black ground with nothing else.
  • The numerals are tubes of glossy, melted metal. Their outlines wobble like poured liquid, and the counters are irregular.
  • The surface reflects white highlights and iridescent violet, blue, cyan, and green, like oil on chrome.
  • The first numeral keeps a flat, square-cut edge on one side, so it reads as a melted solid letter rather than a drawn outline.

Why it belongs

The image isolates the liquid-chrome lettering of the style. It has no acid green and no layout, so it shows that the metal effect alone can carry the look.

Borrow

Render a short word or number as melted iridescent chrome and give it a whole black field.

Keep one straight cut edge on a melted letter so that it still reads as type.
